top_news.title: AI search agents don't fail at searching, they fail at asking the right questions when queries get ambiguous
top_news.dek: AI search agents struggle with ambiguity because they prioritize repeated searching over asking clarifying questions.
top_news.brief: The DiscoBench benchmark reveals that models often fail to identify ambiguous queries, leading to poor research outcomes. Agents that attempt to search repeatedly perform worse than those that guess, with top models achieving only 43 percent accuracy. The findings suggest that agentic workflows need better mechanisms for detecting ambiguity and prompting users for input.
top_news.image_alt: Diagram showing search agent decision paths

top_news.title: LlamaIndex ‘legal-kb’: Agentic Retrieval over Index v2 with retrieve, find, read, and grep Tools
top_news.dek: LlamaIndex released a reference application demonstrating agentic retrieval over document knowledge bases.
top_news.brief: The 'legal-kb' project provides agents with filesystem-like tools including retrieve, find, read, and grep. Built on Index v2, the stack utilizes TanStack Start, AI SDK 6, and Prisma to manage document versioning and visual citations for complex retrieval tasks.

top_news.title: sqlite-utils 4.0rc2, mostly written by Claude Fable (for about $149.25)
top_news.dek: Simon Willison utilized Claude Fable to finalize the 4.0 release of sqlite-utils.
top_news.brief: Willison leveraged Claude Fable to perform a final code review and ensure stability for the sqlite-utils 4.0 release. The experiment highlights the utility of advanced LLMs in maintaining complex open-source projects and adhering to strict versioning standards.

top_news.title: GPT-5.5 Codex reasoning-token clustering may be leading to degraded performance
top_news.dek: Developers report potential performance degradation in GPT-5.5 Codex linked to reasoning-token clustering.
top_news.brief: Discussions on GitHub suggest that specific patterns in reasoning-token generation may be negatively impacting the model's performance on complex coding tasks. The issue highlights concerns regarding how internal reasoning processes influence final output quality in newer model iterations.

primary.title: AI search agents don't fail at searching, they fail at asking the right questions when queries get ambiguous
primary.summary: AI search agents rarely fail at multi-step research because of the search itself. Their real problem is not asking the user for clarification when queries are ambiguous. A new benchmark called DiscoBench shows that models searching repeatedly instead of asking follow-up questions actually perform worse, at 51.9 percent, than those that just guess. Even the best model only hits 43 percent overall accuracy. When ambiguity is removed from the queries, accuracy jumps by up to 40 points.
